operator.dynamic_viscosity: mu_i = restDensity_i * kinematicViscosity_i; mu_ij is the harmonic combination and is zero when either endpoint viscosity is zero.
operator.particle_volume: V_i is explicit restParticleVolume_i when positive and cubic particle diameter otherwise; V_ij is the harmonic combination.
operator.pair_force: F_ij = mu_ij * V_ij * max(1 - distance / maxSupport, 0) * (v_j - v_i).
operator.balance: One common force is divided by endpoint physical particle mass with opposite signs; enabled acceleration limits clamp the common force before division.
operator.equal_material_limit: Matching materials and particle volumes reduce exactly to the established kinematicViscosity * q * relativeVelocity acceleration.
operator.dissipation: Pair power is -mu_ij * V_ij * q * squaredRelativeSpeed and is therefore non-positive.
operator.advertisement: No miscible capability is advertised and valid different-material graph requests remain unsupported.

fixtures.analytic_pair: Unequal density, support, radius, explicit particle volume and kinematic viscosity are checked against the closed-form common force and inverse-mass endpoint accelerations.
fixtures.zero_limit: One inviscid endpoint and two inviscid endpoints both produce exactly zero cross-viscous force.
fixtures.endpoint_order: Swapping endpoint populations and material records preserves every physical particle acceleration.
fixtures.population_sweeps: Second-endpoint particle ratios 1, 2 and 4 run at timesteps 0.001, 0.01 and 0.05 seconds.
fixtures.invariants: Every active sweep produces non-vacuous exchange, conserves mass-weighted linear momentum and does not increase mass-weighted kinetic energy.
